 J U D G M E N T

This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of .10,00,000/- along with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by the petitioner.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 08.06.2023 at about 08.30 p.m., accident was caused near Swamy Petrol Bunk, Madanayakanahalli, due to rash and negligent driving of driver of motorcycle bearing registration number KA-52-U-6494 when petitioner was riding his Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-02-EP-3622 on Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-48 Service Road and due to said accident, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Thereafter, he was shifted to Life Line Hospital, Madanayakanahalli and then shifted to ESI Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent a sum of .1,00,000/- towards medical, food, nourishment,
conveyance and other incidental expenses.

Prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and he was Tailor and earning a sum of .22,000/-
per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by its rider.
The respondents, being insurer and owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. On service of notice, respondent No.1 appeared before the tribunal through their counsel and filed their written statement.
The respondent No.2 did not appeared before the tribunal and hence he has been placed as exparte.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.1 has specifically denied the contents of claim petition.
The respondent No.1 has denied the age, occupation and income, place, time and manner of accident, involvement of offending vehicle and injuries sustained by the petitioner.
The respondent No.1 has contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
This respondent is the insurer of motor cycle and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
Further contended that the Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-52-U-6494 was not at all involved in the alleged accident.
Further the petitioner himself was solely responsible for alleged accident.
Further contended that the petitioner was not wearing the helmet as on the date of accident.
Further contended that the rider of motor cycle was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office has framed the following:

sentences.text: Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 08.06.2023 at about 08.30 p.m., near Swamy Petrol Bunk, Bengaluru - Tumkur NH-48 Service Road, Madanayakanahalli, while he was riding his Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-02-EP-3622, due to the rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-52-U-6494 by its rider?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6.

In order to prove the contentions of the petition, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and examined Dr.S.A.Somashekara, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12 and closed his side of evidence.
The respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary.

7. Heard the arguments on both the sides and perused the materials available on record.
8.

This Tribunal answers the above issues as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative;
 Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:-

9. Issue No.1:- The petitioner contended that on 08.06.2023 at about 08.30 p.m., near Swamy Petrol Bunk, Bengaluru - Tumkur NH - 48 Service Road, Madanayakanahalli, while he was riding his Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-02-EP-3622, due to the rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-52-U-6494 by its rider, accident was caused in which he sustained grievous injuries.
10.
In order to prove rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-52-U-6494 by its rider, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1.
In his chief examination he has deposed that due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by its rider the accident occurred.
On perusal of cross- examination of PW.1 nothing has been elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disprove the case of petitioner.
11. Further, in order to prove accident, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.1 & 2, FIR and first information.

On perusal of Ex.P.2 first information, complainant himself lodged complaint with the Harish vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177583240/
3 police on 08.06.2023.

sentences.text: After registering the case, the police went near the place of accident and drew spot panchanama as per Ex.P.3 by narrating the place of accident.
Ex.P.4 - IMV Report, wherein mentioned the damages caused to both the vehicles.
Ex. P.5 - Wound certificate, it shows that petitioner has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident.

After investigation police filed charge sheet, as per Ex.P.8, against rider of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 338 of IPC.
12.
The FIR as well as complaint discloses that allegation of rashness and negligence is made against the rider of motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-52-U-6494.
In the said documents, it is stated that rash and negligent driving of offending motorcycle, by its driver, is the cause for the accident.
The police appears to have conducted the investigation, after registering the FIR, by visiting the place of incident which aspect could be noticed through Ex.P.3.
The owner or rider of offending motorcycle does not appear to have challenged the FIR.
Allegations are made against the rider of offending vehicle which does not appear to have been challenged.

After conclusion of investigation,
the police appears to have filed the final report against the rider of offending vehicle as per Ex.P.8.
The final report is filed for the offence punishable under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC against the rider of offending vehicle.
The contents of final report disclose the aspect of rashness and negligence on the part of rider of offending motorcycle in the cause of accident.
It is mentioned in Ex.P.8 that the accident was caused due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle.
The final report is filed by the concerned police after detailed investigation and same does not appear to have been challenged either by owner or by rider of the offending vehicle.
13. The petitioner got examined as PW.1 and filed the affidavit in lieu of chief examination wherein he reiterated the contentions of the petition.
PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondent No.1.
In the cross examination also, nothing to doubt the negligence of rider of offending vehicle in the cause of accident, could be elicited from the witness.
Though PW.1 is cross examined, nothing to doubt or dispute the contention of petitioner related to the negligence of offending vehicle could be elicited.

Nothing contrary to the contention of petition and the documents related to negligence of offending vehicle, could be elicited in the cross examination of PW.1.
14.
The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be relied upon for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The materials placed by the petitioner disclose the aspect of negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle in the cause of accident.
On perusal of entire record, the rider of insured vehicle, driven the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner's vehicle.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P-1 to P-8, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-52-U-6494 by its rider and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative.
15. Issue No.2:
In view of held issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury,
pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical Harish vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177583240/
4 expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.
i) Towards injury, pain and suffering:- The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained injuries and underwent surgery and later, discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment.
In order to prove the injuries sustained, the petitioner produced Wound certificate issued by Life Line Hospital which is marked as Ex.P.5.
The wound certificate discloses that the injuries sustained by petitioner are grievous in nature.
The documents furnished by petitioner disclose that he took treatment in hospital as an inpatient.

The petitioner furnished Discharge Summaries issued by Lifeline and ESI Hospitals which is marked as Ex.P6 &
7.

The petitioner examined Dr.S.A.Somashekara as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P11 & 12.
PW.2/doctor deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and stated that petitioner having physical disability of lower limb to the extent of 42% and to the whole body at 21%.

On consideration of facts and circumstances of the case and nature of the injuries, the tribunal is of the view that the compensation of .50,000/- appears just and reasonable towards pain and suffering.
(ii) Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioner claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that he took treatment at the Hospital for the injuries sustained by him.
The petitioner has produced Medical bills which are marked as Ex.P.10.
Ex. P.10
discloses expenditure of .37,512/- towards medical expenses.
The respondent not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or disprove the said document.
PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondent and in the cross examination also, nothing to rebut or doubt the medical bills, is elicited.
The respondents not rebutted the medical bills by placing cogent evidence.
So, this tribunal is of the view that compensation of .37,512/- appears just and reasonable towards medical expenses.
(iii) Towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges:
On perusal of records, the accident occurred on 08.06.2023 and the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient in the hospital.
On perusal of evidence, the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient at Hospital due to the injuries sustained by him.
During the time of treatment, the petitioner might have also required good food and extra nourishment.

The petitioner produced Ex.P.6 & 7 - Discharge Summaries issued by Life Line & ESI Hospitals, wherein it discloses that petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient from 08.06.2023 to 27.06.2023 i.e., for a period of 20 days.

Considering the said facts, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .500/- per day for 20 days to a sum of .10,000/- appears just and reasonable towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant.
(iv) Towards Conveyance:

The petitioner is the resident of Harokyatanahalli, Makali Post, Dasanapura Hobli,
Bengaluru Rural.
The petitioner got admitted to hospital for availing treatment.
Ex. P.6

& 7,

sentences.text: The petitioner might have incurred expenses towards conveyance during the period of treatment.
Considering the nature of injuries and facts of the case, the tribunal is of view that the compensation of .10,000/- appears just and proper towards conveyance charges.
(v) Towards loss of income during treatment:
The petitioner contended that he was a Tailor and earning a sum of .22,000/- per month.
In order to prove his income, the petitioner not produced any documents.
The petitioner not placed any satisfactory materials to show that he was earning .22,000/- per month.
No materials are placed by the petitioner in order to substantiate his contentions related to his occupation and income.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, notional income needs to be taken into consideration.
On consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as .16,000/-.
On perusal of records, it appears that petitioner might not attended his work for some time due to accidental injuries.
The medical records disclose the aspect of petitioner being admitted to the hospital due to the injuries.
The petitioner might not have attended his work during the period of treatment and subsequently also for certain period.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for .30,000/- towards loss of income during treatment.
(vi) Towards Loss of future earning capacity:
The petitioner contended that due to accident, he was admitted as an inpatient at hospital, and sustained permanent disablement.

The petitioner also examined Dr.S.A.Somashekara, working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital,
Bengaluru as PW.2.
PW.2/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically to assess disabilities.

The doctor deposed that petitioner has sustained left distal femur type I open commuted fracture and he underwent surgery in the form of open reduction internal fixation with distal femur lateral plating under SAB and later discharged.
The doctor has examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and assessed the disability to lower limb to the extent of 42% and to the whole body at 21%.
In order to prove the disability, doctor has produced Ex.P.11 & 12 i.e., OPD Record and X-ray film.
PW.2 deposed that the petitioner complained about difficult to squat, sit cross legged and complained to have pain while climbing stairs.
PW.2 also stated that there is difficulty for the petitioner to do his work.
The petitioner is stated to be doing tailoring work and the injury sustained by him might appear to cause difficulty in doing his work which requires use of lower limbs.

It is not Harish vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177583240/
6 forthcoming from the materials placed before the court that the petitioner is not at all able to do his work.

sentences.text: By considering the oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner can do his work with difficulty and said aspect is stated by PW.2 also in the evidence.
As per ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another and considering facts and circumstances of the case, the functional disability is assessed at 12%.

sentences.text: In order to prove age, the petitioner produced Ex.P.9 - Notarized copy of Aadhaar Card, wherein the date of birth of petitioner is mentioned as 10.10.1978.
The accident occurred on 08.06.2023.
As per Ex.P.9, the age of petitioner is 45 years as on the date of accident.
No materials contrary to the said document are placed before the court.
In the absence of contrary materials, Ex.P.10 is to be relied for ascertaining the age of petitioner as on the date of accident.
As such, based on the materials placed on record, the age of the petitioner is 45 years as on the date of accident and same is taken for consideration for applying multiplier.
As per Smt.Sarla Verma case multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '14'.

As per ratio laid down by Hon'ble supreme court in Raj Kumar V/s.
Ajay kumar and another, this tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of his gross income.

Hence, future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under :
Annual Income before accident : (.16,000/- x 12) = .1,92,000/-
Loss of future earning p.a. (12% of prior annual income) = .23,040/-.
Multiplier applicable with reference to age - 14 Loss of future earnings - (.23,040/- x 14) = .3,22,560/-.
The petitioner is entitled for .3,22,560/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
(vii) Deprivation of Future Amenities:- The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and he is unable to do his day- today activities as earlier.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .10,000/- is just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future amenities.

In MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Page No.7 at Para No.15 held as follows:
"However, the provisions of Section 149(1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to the general law enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law overrides the general law.

sentences.text: Therefore, in the absence of any other law relating to interest on Judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Section 34 of CPC, 1908.

Thus, in the given circumstances of this case,
interest at the rate of more than 6% could not have been awarded."

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above judgment, the petitioner is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

sentences.text: The petitioner has filed petition against the respondents No.1 and 2.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-52-U-6494 by its rider.
So, the respondent No.1 & 2, being the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
19. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, I proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .5,00,072/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Seventy Two only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
(future medical expenses shall not carry any interest).
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioner.
Respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 40% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank and the remaining 60% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal.

Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to his account after expiry of three years period of deposit,
without waiting for further order of court.
The Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
